reading: Each colour has two objects. Objects are regrouped by colour into columns at the bottom-left: the colour whose object is leftmost gets the left column, the next column starts one blank column after the widest object of the previous one. In a column the objects are stacked from the bottom row upward with one blank row between them, the leftmost (in the input) at the bottom, each left-aligned to the column start.
verb: sort and stack objects by colour

slots.column order: colour of the leftmost object first, left to right; column width = widest object + 1 gap
slots.stack order: within a colour, object with smaller min-x goes lower; stacked from bottom row with 1-row gaps, left-aligned

why: output holds exactly the input objects, shapes unchanged, packed into bottom-left colour columns

reading: The grid is 3x3 panels separated by background lines. Each panel holds a piece of one pattern (a corner, an edge middle, or the full pattern); each panel is moved to the slot its piece points to (top-left piece to top-left slot, full pattern to the centre).

slots.units: the 9 panels cut by background separator lines
slots.target slot: the slot given by where the panel's minority-colour cells sit inside the panel (left/centre/right x top/middle/bottom); the panel with all pieces goes to the centre

why: output panels are the input panels permuted; each panel's marked cells lie on the side matching its slot

reading: Panels are cut by full separator lines. A panel crossed by a colour-4 line is mirrored across that line (its two blocks swap sides). A panel without a 4-line has its colour-1 placeholder blocks repainted with the one other block colour in that panel.
verb: mirror key panels, fill placeholder panels

slots.units: panels cut by full separator lines (not by the 4-lines inside a panel)
slots.case A: panel contains a line of 4: mirror the panel about that line
slots.case B: no 4-line: every 1 cell becomes the panel's single non-1 block colour

why: every panel is either symmetric-swapped about its 4-line or uniformly one block colour

reading: Some cells of a woven 1/2 pattern are marked 8. Every other non-zero component that has exactly the same shape (same orientation) as an 8 component is recoloured 8.

new_rows.name: shape_twin
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
omy(O, min(Y)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
omx(O, min(X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
rel(O, DY, DX) :- obj(O, Y, X), omy(O, MY), omx(O, MX), DY = Y - MY, DX = X - MX.
eight(O) :- obj(O, Y, X), cell(Y, X, 8).
cand(O) :- obj(O, Y, X), cell(Y, X, C), C > 0, !eight(O).
miss(O, E) :- cand(O), eight(E), rel(O, DY, DX), !rel(E, DY, DX).
same(O) :- cand(O), eight(E), osize(O, N), osize(E, N), !miss(O, E).
shape_twin(Y, X) :- same(O), obj(O, Y, X).

why: every non-zero, non-8 component whose normalised cell set equals an 8 component's becomes 8 (2->8 or 1->8); nothing else changes

reading: Some rows hold a 1 and, to its right, an 8. For each such row (top to bottom) the cells strictly between the 1 and the 8 are cut out; the strips are stacked into the output.

slots.rows: rows containing both a 1 and an 8, in top-down order
slots.strip: cells strictly between the 1 (left) and the 8 (right) on that row
slots.output: strips stacked vertically (all strips have equal length)

why: output row k equals the input cells between 1 and 8 on the k-th marked row

reading: Partial plus-shaped crosses of 2 are hidden in 5/0 noise. Each cross is completed: its centre is where the horizontal and vertical arms meet, both arms have the same length (the furthest 2 from the centre), and every non-2 cell on the completed cross becomes 8.

slots.subject: groups of 2 cells lying on one row and one column through a common centre
slots.shape: plus with equal arms, arm length = max distance of a 2 from the centre (2 or 3)
slots.paint: 8 on every cell of the plus that is not 2 (was 5 or 0)

why: after the change every cross is a full symmetric plus of 2s and 8s; only cross cells change

reading: Several 6-shapes each have one single-cell marker of another colour near them. Each shape is recoloured with its nearest marker's colour, and the shapes' bounding boxes are placed side by side (left to right when the shapes are spread horizontally, top to bottom when spread vertically) to form the output.
verb: recolour by nearest marker and concatenate

frame.verb: recolour shapes by marker and pack boxes

slots.subject: the 6-coloured objects
slots.key: colour of the nearest single-cell marker
slots.layout: shape boxes concatenated in reading order along the axis the shapes are spread on, markers dropped

why: output is the shapes' boxes, in input order, each shape painted with its marker colour

reading: A diagonal (up-right) segment of 2s of length n sits on the anti-diagonal from the bottom-left corner. It is replaced by the next segment along that diagonal, of length n+1, starting just after where the old one ended; the old segment is erased.

slots.subject: the 2-coloured diagonal segment of length n
slots.new segment: n+1 cells on the same anti-diagonal line, continuing up-right right after the old end

why: output holds one diagonal segment, one cell longer, adjacent beyond the old one on the same line
invariants: diagonal line through the bottom-left corner

reading: A small shape is drawn in 8. Every placement of that shape, rotated by 0/90/180/270 degrees (no reflections), that lies entirely on 3 cells has those cells recoloured 8.

new_rows.name: rot_match
new_rows.datalog:
e8(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 8).
three(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 3).
ry(min(Y)) :- e8(Y, X).
rx(min(X)) :- e8(Y, X).
t0(DY, DX) :- e8(Y, X), ry(MY), rx(MX), DY = Y - MY, DX = X - MX.
t(0, A, B) :- t0(DY, DX), A = DY + 0, B = DX + 0.
t(1, A, B) :- t0(DY, DX), A = DX + 0, B = 0 - DY.
t(2, A, B) :- t0(DY, DX), A = 0 - DY, B = 0 - DX.
t(3, A, B) :- t0(DY, DX), A = 0 - DX, B = DY + 0.
cand(R, AY, AX) :- t(R, DY, DX), three(Y, X), AY = Y - DY, AX = X - DX.
bad(R, AY, AX) :- cand(R, AY, AX), t(R, DY, DX), Y = AY + DY, X = AX + DX, !three(Y, X).
ok(R, AY, AX) :- cand(R, AY, AX), !bad(R, AY, AX).
rot_match(Y, X) :- ok(R, AY, AX), t(R, DY, DX), Y = AY + DY, X = AX + DX.

why: exactly the 3 cells covered by a rotated copy of the 8 shape become 8 (3->8); nothing else changes

reading: Several 3x3 shapes; exactly one contains an 8 cell. The output is that shape's 3x3 box with the 8 replaced by the shape's own colour.
verb: extract marked shape and fill its mark
why: the only multi-coloured component is the shape holding the 8; its box is the output with 8 -> surrounding shape colour
invariants: the chosen shape's cells and box
